prompt:
Image 1 is a reference sheet of one specific person. Image 2 is a club crest.

Photograph THAT EXACT PERSON — same face, same bone structure, same hair, same build,
same age — in full Ice Hockey kit: hockey helmet, gloves, padded jersey, hockey stick, skates.

POSE: seen strictly from behind, winding up for a slapshot with the stick raised behind the shoulder, feet apart and set.
CAMERA: eye level, directly behind the athlete, 85 mm lens, full body.
EQUIPMENT: the raised stick stays entirely inside the frame.

UNIFORM — identical in every pose, this is not a place to improvise: a SOLID navy jersey with no contrast shoulders and no contrast sleeves — the only trim is one red band around the waist hem and a red collar edge; navy breezers, navy socks, black skates, navy gloves, navy helmet with a clear flat visor.
Primary colour #12284B, secondary #C8102E.
The crest from image 2 is on the centre chest of the jersey. COPY IT, do not redraw it:
same outline shape, same figure inside, same colours in the same places, same proportions.
Do not invert the colours, do not add or remove a white field behind it, do not simplify
it and do not add lettering. It is printed onto the fabric, so it creases and shades with
the cloth, but the artwork itself is unchanged. Roughly a hand's width across, and it is
the ONLY graphic on the kit.
The number 17 is printed large across the upper back, legible, in the secondary colour.

This must look like an actual photograph of an actual teenager, taken by a person with
a camera. Skin has visible pore texture, faint blemishes, uneven tone, a flush of blood
where they have been working. Hair is made of separate strands with flyaways that catch
the rim light, not a moulded mass. Eyebrows are uneven. The face is asymmetric, the way
every real face is. Fabric creases, bunches at the joints and darkens where it is damp.
Equipment is used: scuffed, scratched, tape worn at the edges.

Lighting, identical in every shot: a large soft key from camera-left and slightly above,
a hard rim light from behind camera-right that separates the shoulders, helmet and hair
from the backdrop, and a weak fill from below-right. Neutral white balance. No coloured
gels, no arena lighting, no atmosphere, no haze, no lens flare.

Hard requirements — this image will be cut out and composited, so:
- Flat, evenly lit seamless mid-grey (18% grey) studio backdrop, completely plain — no gradient, no vignette, no floor line, no shadow on it, no set.
- The athlete is ALONE and stands on nothing: no ice, no floor, no ground, no rink, no
  arena, no crowd, no other people, no ice spray, no snow, no particles, no smoke.
- FRAMING: leave a clear empty band of backdrop around the athlete on ALL FOUR sides,
  roughly a hand's width at this scale. Nothing may touch or cross a frame edge — not
  the top of the helmet, not a skate, and above all not the far end of the stick, which
  is the thing that gets clipped. If the pose does not fit, PULL THE CAMERA BACK. Never
  change the pose to make it fit and never let anything run off the edge.
- the back of the jersey with the number large and legible across the shoulders, the back of the helmet, no part of the face — not in profile, not over a shoulder.
- Vertical 2:3, the athlete filling most of the height.
- All equipment is UNBRANDED: plain skates, plain stick, plain helmet, plain gloves. No
  manufacturer names, no maker's logos, no swooshes, no model names — not even small or
  faint ones on the boot, the shaft or the shell.
- Sharp throughout. No motion blur, no shallow-focus blur. Keep any contact shadow tight
  under the feet — no long cast shadow stretching across the backdrop, and no visible
  seam where a floor would meet the wall.
- No text, no lettering, no sponsor marks, no brand logos, no watermark — the jersey number and the chest crest are the only exceptions.
- No airbrushed, retouched or beauty-filtered skin. No skin smoothing of any kind.
- No waxy or plastic sheen on the face, no glowing translucent skin, no mannequin look.
- No 3D render, no CGI, no video-game character, no digital sculpt, no illustration.
- No perfectly symmetric face, no flawless white teeth, no poreless skin.
- No brand-new spotless uniform and no factory-fresh equipment.
- Not an adult professional athlete — this is a high-school age player.
